messages:
Aisha K.: FYI support case from a customer in eu-west-1 — their outbound firewall is blocking our edge nodes. They need a concise allowlist and testing steps. Any quick guidance? :thinking_face:

Ryan C.: Do they use a corporate HTTP proxy or full NAT?

Aisha K.: They have a chained proxy + firewall. Proxy requires explicit allowlist of destination IPs and only allows CONNECT to port 443. They also run TLS inspection on some hosts.

SRE Oncall: TL;DR: ask them to allow our region NAT pools + DNS and to avoid TLS-inspect for api hostnames. Key points:
- Allow outgoing TCP 443 to our published NAT ranges for eu-west (we rotate, see runbook link)
- Allow UDP 53 (or TCP 53) to their resolvers OR allow outbound to a trusted DNS provider (we recommend DoT/853 if they use encrypted DNS)
- If they have a proxy doing TLS MITM, it will break SNI-based routing and HTTP/2 features. Recommend exempting the following hostnames from interception: `*.api.redwood-inference.com`, `*.edge.redwood-inference.com`

SRE Oncall: Example minimal ACL snippet (send this as plain text to customers):
```
# allow our eu-west NAT pools (examples)
3.12.240.0/22    443
18.197.32.0/24   443
52.29.128.0/25   443
# DNS
0.0.0.0/0        53 (udp)
# (Optional) DoT
0.0.0.0/0        853 (tcp)
```
Note: those are example CIDRs — we'll provide canonical list via support ticket.

Ryan C.: Also call out ephemeral source port behavior — customers sometimes only allow destination IPs but also do stateful inspection that drops connections if source port changes. Our nodes SNAT outgoing flows; source ports are ephemeral and will vary.

SRE Oncall: Right. Tell them to avoid port-based NAT pinning rules. Also port-preserve NAT is not guaranteed on our side (depends on provider). If they have SNAT port affinity expecting fixed source-port pairs, that will fail under load/batching.

Aisha K.: What about proxy auth? They said proxy requires NTLM for internal hosts but allows anonymous CONNECT for external.

SRE Oncall: We only need CONNECT to our hostnames. If their proxy requires NTLM for outbound CONNECT, the customer's network team must create an exception for the `*.api.redwood-inference.com` domain or map our IP ranges to a no-auth policy. Otherwise requests will fail at proxy handshake.

Maria P.: I'll add a short KB for customers. Can you confirm the testing commands we should give them?

SRE Oncall: Test checklist to include in KB:
- DNS: `dig @<their-resolver> api.redwood-inference.com` -> ensure resolves to public IP
- Proxy CONNECT test: `curl -v --proxy http://<proxy>:3128 https://api.redwood-inference.com/health` -> should get 200/302 depending on config
- Direct TCP test from inside their network: `openssl s_client -connect <one-of-published-ip>:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com` -> verify TLS handshake and that SNI matches
- Check for TLS interception: look for CA in cert chain that is not a public CA or for replaced cert CNs

InfraBot: Note added to internal runbook: "egress-acl-customer-requests" — runbook id #EG-102. (link: internal/runbooks/EG-102)

Aisha K.: Perfect. I'll send the customer: 1) sample CIDRs (from support), 2) exempt hostnames for TLS inspection, 3) proxy CONNECT guidance and tests. Maria — ping me when the KB is up so I can link it in the ticket. :thumbsup:

Maria P.: Will do. Also capturing an FAQ item: "Why do I need to allow UDP 53?" — answer: some workloads do DNS lookups locally; if DNS is blocked they fall back to failures instead of using cache.

Ryan C.: One more note: if they run egress filtering by FQDN (SNI-based firewall), make sure they include both `api.redwood-inference.com` and the regional edge hostnames we provide. Some customers only whitelist `api.*` and miss edge subdomains.

Aisha K.: Thanks all — sending now.
